給事中 is the Supervising Secretary (Chancellery), not an edict drafter.
Directors of the Court of Judicial Review received fourteen thousand cash; directors of various offices and directorates received twelve thousand cash,
Assistants of the Court of Judicial Review received fourteen thousand cash; assistants of the various courts and directorates received twelve thousand cash,

Third-Rank Service appointees and borrowed appointees received four thousand cash.

三班 means the Three Echelons, not 'third rank'.

unresolvedReferences.description: The Zhidao 2 (996) edict on secretaries' salaries names no person; the issuing emperor (Taizong) is not named.
The text does not say which of Wen Yanbo, Lü Gongbi, Feng Jing and Wu Chong held the commissioner post and which the vice-commissioner post, nor their individual dates.
《無豐令》/《無豐格》 are evidently scribal errors for 元豐令/元豐格 (Yuanfeng Statutes/Regulations); the translation already reads Yuanfeng.

The Xining 4 (1071) memorial on raising the salaries of selected officials is attributed only to the Secretariat-Chancellery (中書門下); the memorialist and the approving emperor (Shenzong) are not named.
The Commissioner for Tax and Corvée (租庸使) of early Later Tang Tongguang who proposed half-cash salaries is not named (historically Kong Qian 孔謙); not extracted.
The Qiande 4 (966) and Kaibao 4 (971) edicts are issued by the unnamed reigning emperor (Song Taizu); not extracted.
The Taiping Xingguo 1 (976), Taiping Xingguo 2 (977), Duangong 1 (988) and Chunhua 1 (990) edicts are issued by an unnamed emperor (Taizong); not extracted.
The Xianping and Dazhong Xiangfu edicts (998–1014) are issued by the unnamed reigning emperor (Zhenzong); only s0742 and s0750 are linked to him.

The Xining 4 (1071) memorial on raising grain allowances is attributed only to the Secretariat-Chancellery; the approving emperor (Shenzong) is not named. Its figures (376 magistrates; 2,513 lower officials) differ from the parallel cash memorial in s0484ff. (367; 2,153)—an internal numerical discrepancy, not a date conflict.
文明殿學士 is glossed in the source as 'i.e. Guanwen' (即觀文), and 次政殿 in s0975 is evidently a scribal error for 資政殿; noted, not repaired.
